teaser.text: Apple sells devices, software and services that fit together into a single customer relationship. A dollar enters when a customer or business partner buys a product, access or a transaction, and leaves as Apple pays suppliers, workers, content providers and other operating costs before keeping the remainder.

stock.title: Apple Inc. stock forecast: weighted case
stock.meta_description: Apple Inc. stock forecast: the weighted case is $315.27 in October 2027 and $313.03 in October 2029, with key drivers and valuation.
stock.opening: The weighted scenario is $315.27 in October 2027, a 6% loss. It hinges on profitable AI and Services growth.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Apple Inc.’s business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Apple Inc.'s shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: It is $315.38 in October 2028. The October 2029 weighted price is $313.03, also a 6% loss with dividends. The last-date range runs from $193.85 in the bear case to $453.79 in the bull case. Today’s supplied price is $336.64.

Bear probability is 25%; base is 55%. Bull probability is 20%. iPhone Duo preorders begin October 16 and availability begins October 23. Another market expansion is scheduled for October 30. Completed deliveries, cancellations and returns matter more than wait times alone. Apple promised to expand Siri AI beyond English during October; repeated use and upgrade behavior will show whether it matters. The view improves if supply constraints ease, premium upgrades hold and Services growth supports cash generation. It weakens if memory costs rise, refunds fade and demand slows. Apple’s installed base creates value only if AI and Services turn it into durable cash growth.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Apple Inc., and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: Base P/E falls from 33x to 31x, then 29x. Bear valuation contracts from 28x to 25x and then 22x as growth and platform economics weaken. Bull valuation holds at 36x before easing to 35x, requiring evidence that AI produces profitable upgrades and that Services growth remains durable. Services had a 75.4% gross margin in 2025, versus 36.8% for Products.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Apple Inc. really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is cash from operations after spending on long-term assets. Apple generated $111,482 million from operations in 2025. After capital spending, free cash flow was $98,767 million, or 23.7% of revenue. That was below the prior year despite higher earnings, so one year’s cash conversion needs explanation.

Stock compensation is not an immediate cash payment, so Apple adds it back in operating cash flow. But it gives employees claims on the business. Deducting $12,863 million of stock pay leaves “real free cash flow” of $85,904 million, or 20.6% of revenue. That is an analytical measure, not Apple’s reported one, and it should not be deducted twice.

dividend.title: Apple Inc. dividend: cash coverage and outlook
dividend.meta_description: Apple Inc.'s dividend is covered by free cash flow, while buybacks, the current yield and business risks shape its outlook.
dividend.opening: Apple Inc.'s forecast dividend rises from $1.10 per share to $1.18. In 2025, $98,767 million of free cash flow covered the $15,421 million dividend, but not the $106,132 million total shareholder payout.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains Apple Inc.'s business, rivals, management decisions and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Apple Inc. pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend rises from $1.10 per share to $1.14, then $1.18. That follows five years of increases and management’s stated intention to raise the dividend annually. The bear case holds each period at $1.08, while the bull case reaches $1.24 as stronger cash generation permits faster increases.

blocks.heading: Is Apple Inc.'s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: From fiscal 2021 through fiscal 2025, Apple generated $511,554 million of free cash flow and paid shareholders $513,571 million. In 2025, it generated $98,767 million but distributed $106,132 million. Buybacks accounted for $90,711 million and dividends for $15,421 million. A buyback purchases shares from sellers, reducing the number remaining; that can increase each remaining share’s claim on profits, but only if Apple does not overpay or sacrifice better investments.

blocks.heading: What is Apple Inc.'s dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: Revenue recovered in fiscal 2025 after declining in 2023, while operating margin rose across the five-year period. Computed free cash flow—as cash from operations minus capital spending—as a share of revenue fell in 2025 even as earnings increased; net debt declined from its 2022 level. Apple’s share price is $336.64. Trailing P/E is 38.6x; forward P/E is 35.0x. Free cash flow yield is 2.0%; real free cash flow yield is 1.7%.

earnings.title: Apple Inc. earnings: date, guidance and results
earnings.meta_description: Apple Inc. expects results on November 2, 2026; guidance covers growth, margin and expenses, with deliveries and AI use to watch.
earnings.opening: Apple Inc.'s next results are expected on November 2, 2026. Watch completed deliveries, cancellations and returns for evidence of demand rather than supply limits.
earnings.closing: The full memo also covers Apple Inc.'s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has Apple Inc. guided for the September quarter?

paragraphs.text: Management guides to revenue growth of 9–11% for the September 2026 quarter and iPhone revenue growth in the mid-teens. It forecasts gross margin of 47–48%, including about one percentage point from tariff refunds, while rising memory costs could pressure the underlying margin. Forecast operating expenses are $19.1–19.4 billion.

blocks.heading: Did Apple Inc. keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Finally, Apple promised a more personalized Siri in 2024, acknowledged a delay in March 2025 and introduced Siri AI for developer testing on June 8, 2026. A beta is a testing release, not full delivery. Apple’s leaders are therefore on shareholders’ side only if strong returns, disciplined dilution and reliable products arrive together.

blocks.heading: What do Apple Inc.'s last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: For the quarter ended June 27, 2026, revenue reached $109,417 million, up about 16.4%. Growth was broad: iPhone, Mac, Services and Wearables, Home and Accessories increased, while iPad declined. Pro iPhones and Mac laptops helped drive the result, and Services continued to benefit from advertising and cloud spending.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in Apple Inc.'s next results?

paragraphs.text: The next useful signals are completed deliveries, wider AI availability and the rules governing App Store income. September results will show whether Apple met its growth and margin promises after tariff refunds. They should also reveal whether component shortages delayed sales into a later quarter rather than destroyed demand.

Product availability will help separate demand from supply problems. Apple scheduled iPhone Duo preorders for October 16 and initial availability for October 23, with another market expansion on October 30. Long waits alone cannot prove popularity because limited supply can create them. Completed deliveries, cancellations and returns will be more informative. Apple also promised to expand Siri AI beyond English during October.
